title: A normalized convex–concave minimax equality
statement:
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ be nonempty, compact, convex sets, and let $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ be jointly continuous on $X \times Y$ and normalized so that $0 \le f(x,y) \le 1$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Suppose that $f$ is bounded above and below on $X \times Y$, that for every $y \in Y$ the map $x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous and convex on $X$, and that for every $x \in X$ the map $y \mapsto f(x,y)$ is concave on $Y$. Then
\[
  \inf_{x \in X}\,\sup_{y \in Y}\,f(x,y)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{y \in Y}\,\inf_{x \in X}\,f(x,y).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f jointly continuous on X × Y
f(·,y) continuous on X for each y
f(·,y) convex on X for each y
f(x,·) concave on Y for each x
f bounded above on X × Y
f bounded below on X × Y
replaced:
Under the convex-compact minimax hypotheses, if additionally $Y$ is compact, $f$ is
jointly continuous on $X \times Y$, and $0 \le f \le 1$, then the minimax equality
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y)
    = \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y)
\]
holds.
